title: Aligned population, endpoint and follow-up but still separate trials

patient_context.chief_complaint: The separate studies now use the same population, endpoint and follow-up. Is A proven superior because 62% exceeds 48%?
patient_context.history: Controlled fixture: design dimensions are aligned across two independent trials, but participants were not randomized within one direct A-versus-B comparison.

interaction.prompt: Assess how much stronger the indirect comparison becomes when major design dimensions align, while distinguishing aligned separate studies from randomized head-to-head evidence.

must_include: Recognize that alignment improves interpretability of the descriptive difference.
Still distinguish separate trial contexts from direct randomized comparison.
Avoid categorical superiority language unless the fixture provides direct comparative evidence.
must_not_claim: Do not describe the studies as head-to-head.
Do not respond with blanket 'nothing can ever be compared' language that ignores improved alignment.
acceptable_actions: Describe A's numerically higher result as stronger indirect evidence but not direct proof of superiority.
expected_behavior.uncertainty_behavior: Reduce uncertainty relative to unmatched trials but preserve the direct-versus-indirect distinction.

forbidden_claims: aligned separate studies are randomized head-to-head evidence
no meaningful descriptive comparison is possible at all

critical_errors: Mislabels aligned separate studies as direct randomized evidence.
